5. **Captions:** on, off, switching languages, and position while the controls hide.
6. **Preferences:** `prefers-reduced-motion`, `forced-colors`, and 200% browser zoom.
7. **Skin switching:** `player.setSkin(other())` and back leaves no stray elements or attributes.

Inside the monorepo, `pnpm playground` builds everything and serves a page where you can try your skin, and `pnpm validate && pnpm test && pnpm size` must pass before a pull request.

## 10. Package and publish

### Inside the Tomato Player monorepo

```sh
pnpm new skin aurora "Streaming and course skin with skip intro and HTML captions"
pnpm install
pnpm --filter @tomato-player/skin-aurora build
pnpm validate && pnpm test
```

This scaffolds `packages/skins/aurora` from `templates/skin` with a validated `package.json`. Open a pull request with the **New skin** template. See [Create a skin](create-a-skin.md) for the short version.

### As your own npm package

Name community skins `tomato-player-skin-<name>` and add the `tomato-player-skin` keyword so they are easy to find. Layout:

```
tomato-player-skin-aurora/
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts
│   ├── style.css
│   └── css.d.ts
├── test/aurora.test.ts
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── README.md
└── LICENSE
```

`package.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "tomato-player-skin-aurora",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "description": "Aurora: a Tomato Player skin for streaming and course platforms.",
  "license": "MIT",
  "type": "module",
  "sideEffects": ["*.css"],
  "main": "./dist/index.cjs",
  "module": "./dist/index.js",
  "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "types": "./dist/index.d.ts",
      "import": "./dist/index.js",
      "require": "./dist/index.cjs"
    },
    "./style.css": "./dist/style.css"
  },
  "files": ["dist", "LICENSE"],
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsup src/index.ts --format esm,cjs --dts --clean --minify --loader .css=text && cp src/style.css dist/style.css",
    "test": "vitest run",
    "prepublishOnly": "npm run build && npm test"
  },
  "peerDependencies": {
    "@tomato-player/core": "^0.1.0",
    "@tomato-player/ui": "^0.1.0"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@tomato-player/core": "^0.1.0",
    "@tomato-player/ui": "^0.1.0",
    "happy-dom": "^20.0.0",
    "tsup": "^8.3.5",
    "typescript": "^5.6.3",
    "vitest": "^3.0.0"
  },
  "keywords": ["tomato-player", "tomato-player-skin", "video", "player", "skin"]
}
```

Why this shape:

- **`@tomato-player/core` is a peer dependency.** The app owns the player. Your skin must use the same core instance and types, not a second copy. List `@tomato-player/ui` as a peer too, so the controls and base stylesheet come from the same version the app's other skins use. tsup leaves peer dependencies out of the bundle automatically.
- **The CSS is shipped twice:** inlined as a string in the JavaScript, for automatic injection, and as `dist/style.css`, for strict-CSP users who set `injectStyles: false` and import it themselves.
- **`sideEffects: ["*.css"]`** lets bundlers tree-shake the JavaScript but keep CSS imports.
- **ESM, CJS and types** match the official packages, so the skin works in Vite, webpack, Next.js and Node-based test runners.

`tsconfig.json`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "Bundler",
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"],
    "strict": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "isolatedModules": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  },
  "include": ["src"]
}
```

Then:

```sh
npm run build
npm publish --access public
```

In your README, include a screenshot, the install command, every option with its default, the tokens your skin reads or adds, and the class names you consider public. Follow semver: renaming a public class or removing an option is a breaking change.

## 11. Use your skin from React, Vue, Svelte and HTML

A skin from a package works exactly like an official skin. Every binding accepts a `Skin` object and calls `setSkin()` when it changes.

### React and Next.js

```tsx
'use client';
import { TomatoPlayer } from '@tomato-player/react';
import { aurora } from 'tomato-player-skin-aurora';

const skin = aurora({ intro: { start: 5, end: 62 } }); // create once, outside render

export function Episode({ src }: { src: string }) {
  return <TomatoPlayer src={src} title="Episode 3" skin={skin} tokens={{ accent: '#38bdf8' }} />;
}
```

Create the skin outside the component or in `useMemo`. A new skin object on every render remounts the skin. `TomatoPlayer` accepts every `createPlayer` option as a prop. Changing `src` or `skin` updates the live player. Other options, such as `tokens`, are read once when the player is created.

### Vue 3 and Nuxt

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { TomatoPlayer } from '@tomato-player/vue';
import { aurora } from 'tomato-player-skin-aurora';

const skin = aurora({ rates: [1, 1.5, 2] });
</script>

<template>
  <TomatoPlayer src="/media/lecture.mp4" title="Lecture 4" :skin="skin" :options="{ tokens: { accent: '#16a34a' } }" />
</template>
```

### Svelte and SvelteKit

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { tomato } from '@tomato-player/svelte';
  import { aurora } from 'tomato-player-skin-aurora';
  const skin = aurora();
</script>

<div use:tomato={{ src: '/media/lecture.mp4', skin, tokens: { accent: '#16a34a' } }} />
```

### Web component and plain HTML

The `<tomato-player>` element's `skin` attribute only knows the nine official skins. For a custom skin, start with `skin="none"` and set it from script:

```html
<tomato-player id="ep3" src="/media/episode-3.mp4" title="Episode 3" skin="none"></tomato-player>

<script type="module">
  import 'tomato-player/element';
  import { aurora } from 'tomato-player-skin-aurora';

  const el = document.getElementById('ep3');
  const apply = (player) => player.setSkin(aurora());
  el.player ? apply(el.player) : el.addEventListener('ready', (e) => apply(e.detail), { once: true });
</script>
```

Don't change the `skin` attribute afterwards. It switches back to an official skin.

Without a bundler, the CDN bundle exposes the UI primitives as `TomatoPlayer.ui`, so a small skin can be written inline:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/playlikeboy/tomato-player@cdn/tomato-player.global.js"></script>
<div id="player"></div>
<script>
  const { createSkin, gestureLayer, spinner, bigPlayButton, group, timeSlider, playButton, timeDisplay, spacer, fullscreenButton } = TomatoPlayer.ui;
  const tiny = createSkin({
    name: 'tiny',
    css: ".tp[data-skin='tiny'] .tp-controls { position: absolute; inset: auto 0 0 0; padding: 8px; background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6); }",
    build: (p) => [
      gestureLayer(p),
      spinner(),
      bigPlayButton(p),
      group('tp-controls tp-autohide tp-hide-unstarted', timeSlider(p), group('tp-row', playButton(p), timeDisplay(p), spacer(), fullscreenButton(p))),
    ],
  });
  TomatoPlayer.createPlayer('#player', { src: '/media/movie.mp4', skin: tiny() });
</script>
```

## 12. Reference

### Classes

Public class names from `@tomato-player/ui`. Style these freely, scoped to your skin.

| Element | Classes |
| --- | --- |
| Root and media | `.tp`, `.tp-media` (the `<video>`), `.tp-skin` (skin container) |
| Layout | `.tp-row`, `.tp-spacer`, `.tp-autohide`, `.tp-hide-unstarted`, `.tp-controls` (convention only, not styled by base) |
| Buttons | `.tp-button`, `.tp-icon`, `.tp-button-text`, `.tp-play`, `.tp-mute`, `.tp-fullscreen`, `.tp-pip`, `.tp-captions`, `.tp-settings`, `.tp-cast`, `.tp-rate`, `.tp-unmute`, `.tp-seek` with `.tp-seek-back` or `.tp-seek-forward`, `.tp-seek-amount` |
| Sliders | `.tp-slider`, `.tp-slider-track`, `.tp-slider-buffer`, `.tp-slider-fill`, `.tp-slider-thumb`, `.tp-time-slider`, `.tp-volume`, `.tp-volume-slider` |
| Seek preview | `.tp-preview`, `.tp-preview-thumb`, `.tp-preview-chapter`, `.tp-preview-time`, `.tp-chapter-markers`, `.tp-chapter-marker` |
| Text | `.tp-time-display`, `.tp-time`, `.tp-time-current`, `.tp-time-duration`, `.tp-time-remaining`, `.tp-time-sep`, `.tp-title`, `.tp-live`, `.tp-live-dot` |
| Overlays | `.tp-gesture-layer`, `.tp-big-play`, `.tp-spinner`, `.tp-spinner-ring`, `.tp-error`, `.tp-error-message`, `.tp-caption`, `.tp-caption-text` |
| Menu | `.tp-menu-wrap`, `.tp-menu`, `.tp-menu-item`, `.tp-menu-label`, `.tp-menu-hint`, `.tp-menu-back` |

Element-level attributes: `.tp-slider[data-dragging]` while dragging, `.tp-preview[data-visible]` while hovering the time slider, `.tp-live[data-edge]` within 10 s of the live edge, `.tp-time-display[data-live]` on live streams.

### State attributes

Set on the `.tp` root:

| Attribute | Present when |
| --- | --- |
| `data-skin="<name>"` | A skin is mounted. |
| `data-ready` | Metadata has loaded. |
| `data-started` | Playback has started at least once for this source. |
| `data-paused` / `data-playing` | Paused / playing (exactly one is set). |
| `data-ended` | Playback reached the end. |
| `data-waiting` | Buffering. Show a spinner. |
| `data-seeking` | A seek is in progress. |
| `data-idle` | No user activity for `idleTimeout` ms during playback. |
| `data-muted` | Muted. |
| `data-live` | Live stream. |
| `data-captions` | A text track is showing. |
| `data-error` | A playback error occurred. |
| `data-fullscreen` | In fullscreen, including pseudo-fullscreen. |
| `data-pseudo-fullscreen` | Pinned to the viewport by `fullscreenFallback: 'pseudo'`. |
| `data-pip` | In picture-in-picture. |
| `data-size="sm\|md\|lg"` | Always. Width under 480 px, under 960 px, or larger. |
| `data-menu-open` | The settings menu is open. |
| `data-muted-autoplay` | Playing muted after `autoplayInView` started it. |

The root is also a size container (`container-type: inline-size`), so `@container` queries and `cqw` units work inside skins.

### Tokens

See the [token table](#4-theme-with-design-tokens) above. Internal properties you should read but not set: `--tp-slider-value` and `--tp-slider-buffer` (0 to 1, set on each slider) and `--tp-preview-x` (preview position).

<!-- source: docs/guides/create-a-skin.md -->

# Create a skin

Skins are the heart of Tomato Player, and anyone can publish one. This page is the short workflow inside the monorepo. For the full guide (tokens, CSS overrides, layout, auto-hide, sizes, menus, captions, portrait, accessibility, testing, publishing to npm and a complete worked example), read [Custom skins: the complete guide](custom-skins.md).

## 1. Scaffold

```sh
pnpm new skin aurora "Northern-lights inspired skin with soft gradients"
pnpm install
```

This creates `packages/skins/aurora` with `src/index.ts`, `src/style.css`, a README and a validated `package.json`.

## 2. Compose controls

```ts
import { createSkin, group, playButton, timeSlider, timeDisplay, spacer, fullscreenButton, bigPlayButton, spinner, gestureLayer } from '@tomato-player/ui';
import css from './style.css';

export const aurora = createSkin<{ glow?: boolean }>({
  name: 'aurora',
  css,
  tokens: { accent: '#34d399' },
  build: (p, root, o) => [
    gestureLayer(p),
    spinner(),
    bigPlayButton(p),
    group('tp-controls tp-autohide tp-hide-unstarted',
      timeSlider(p),
      group('tp-row', playButton(p), timeDisplay(p), spacer(), fullscreenButton(p)),
    ),
  ],
});
```

- `tp-autohide` fades the element out while playing and idle.
- `tp-hide-unstarted` hides it until the first play.
- Return a `{ controls, cleanup }` object if you set up observers or timers.

## 3. Style

Scope **every** selector to your skin. `pnpm validate` enforces it, so skins never leak into each other:

```css
.tp[data-skin='aurora'] { --tp-radius: 16px; }
.tp[data-skin='aurora'] .tp-controls { position: absolute; inset: auto 0 0 0; padding: 32px 12px 8px; }
.tp[data-skin='aurora'][data-waiting] .tp-slider-fill { animation: pulse 1s infinite; }
```

Use state attributes (`data-paused`, `data-idle`, `data-size`…) and `@container` queries rather than JS for visual behavior.

## 4. Custom controls

Any `{ el, destroy }` object is a control:

```ts
function sleepTimer(p: Player): Control {
  const el = h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'tp-button', 'aria-label': 'Sleep in 15 minutes' }, '15m');
  let t: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>;
  el.onclick = () => { clearTimeout(t); t = setTimeout(() => p.pause(), 15 * 60_000); };
  return { el, destroy: () => { clearTimeout(t); el.remove(); } };
}
```

## 5. Checklist

- [ ] Every button has an accessible name (tests check this).
- [ ] Works at 320 px wide (`data-size="sm"`) and in fullscreen.
- [ ] Touch targets ≥ 44 px on `pointer: coarse`.
- [ ] Focus ring visible on every control.
- [ ] No third-party logos, fonts or trademarks. Inspired designs must be labeled "unofficial".
- [ ] `pnpm validate && pnpm test && pnpm size` pass.

## 6. Publish

Inside this monorepo, open a PR using the **New skin** template. Outside it, publish as `tomato-player-skin-<name>` with the `tomato-player-skin` keyword so the gallery can discover it, and declare `@tomato-player/core` as a peer dependency. The [complete guide](custom-skins.md#10-package-and-publish) has a ready `package.json`.


<!-- source: docs/guides/create-a-plugin.md -->

# Create a plugin

```sh
pnpm new plugin sleep-timer "Pause playback after a chosen number of minutes"
```

## Anatomy

```ts
import { definePlugin } from '@tomato-player/core';

export interface SleepTimerAPI { start(minutes: number): void; cancel(): void }

export const sleepTimer = (opts: { defaultMinutes?: number } = {}) =>
  definePlugin<SleepTimerAPI>({
    name: 'sleep-timer',
    setup(player) {
      let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
      const api: SleepTimerAPI = {
        start(min) { clearTimeout(timer); timer = setTimeout(() => player.pause(), min * 60_000); },
        cancel() { clearTimeout(timer); },
      };
      const off = player.on('sourcechange', api.cancel);
      return { api, destroy: () => { off(); api.cancel(); } };
    },
  });
```

## Rules

1. **Clean up everything** in `destroy()`: listeners, timers, DOM, observers. Players are created and destroyed constantly in SPAs.
2. **No work at import time.** Touch `window` and `document` only inside `setup`.
3. **Be SSR-safe and feature-detect.** Return early if an API is missing.
4. **Talk through the player**, not to other plugins: `player.emit('plugin:my-event', data)`, `player.provide(key, api)`, `player.inject(key)`.
5. **Stay small.** The budget is 1.5 KB gzip. Lazy-load heavy SDKs with `import()`.
6. **Never break playback.** Event handlers run inside try/catch, but async errors are yours to handle.

## Testing

```ts
const player = createPlayer(document.body.appendChild(document.createElement('div')), { plugins: [sleepTimer()] });
player.plugin<SleepTimerAPI>('sleep-timer')!.start(1);
```

Run `pnpm test`. Tests use Vitest and happy-dom against source files, so no build is needed.


<!-- source: docs/guides/create-a-provider.md -->

# Create a provider

Providers adapt a playback engine or a media platform (Shaka, mpegts.js, WebRTC/WHEP, an iframe API…) to the player.

```ts
import { defineProvider, type Provider } from '@tomato-player/core';

export const mpegts = (): Provider =>
  defineProvider({
    name: 'mpegts',
    canPlay: (source) => source.type === 'video/mp2t' || /\.flv($|\?)/.test(source.src),
    async create({ media, update, player }) {
      const { default: mpegtsjs } = await import('mpegts.js'); // lazy, code-split
      let engine: any;
      return {
        load(source) {
          engine = mpegtsjs.createPlayer({ type: 'flv', url: source.src, isLive: true });
          engine.attachMediaElement(media);
          engine.load();
          update({ live: true });
        },
        destroy() {
          engine?.destroy();
        },
      };
    },
  });
```

Guidelines:

- `canPlay` must be cheap and synchronous. Check MIME type, extension and browser support (`supportsMSE()`).
- Declare the engine as an **optional peer dependency**, never as a dependency.
- Report qualities, audio tracks, live state and fatal errors through `update()` and `player.emit('error', …)`.
- `destroy()` must release the MediaSource and every network request.


<!-- source: docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

### Autoplay doesn't start

Browsers block autoplay **with sound**. `autoplay: true` tries unmuted playback first and falls back to muted. To always autoplay, pass `muted: true` and show an unmute control (`unmuteButton()`, or the Feed and Campus skins). Autoplay also needs `playsInline` on iOS, which is on by default.

### `NotAllowedError: play() failed because the user didn't interact`

Call `player.play()` from a user gesture (click or keydown), or play muted.

### My custom controls disappear in fullscreen on iPhone

iPhone Safari only supports fullscreen on the `<video>` element, which shows the native UI. Use `fullscreenFallback: 'pseudo'` to keep your skin by pinning the player to the viewport. iPadOS supports element fullscreen and is unaffected.

### `NO_PROVIDER` error

You passed a `.mpd` (DASH) without `providers: [dash()]`, or an `.m3u8` on a browser without native HLS and without `providers: [hls()]`. If the URL has no extension, set the type: `{ src, type: 'application/x-mpegurl' }`.

### `SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED`

The URL returned an error (403/404), or the browser can't decode the codec (for example HEVC on Firefox, or H.264 in some Chromium builds). Open the URL directly and check the Network panel.

### Captions or thumbnails don't load from another domain

Text tracks and fetches are subject to CORS. Serve them with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and set `crossOrigin: 'anonymous'` on the player.

### `window is not defined` / hydration mismatch (Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit)

No Tomato Player package touches the DOM at import time. If you see this, you are calling `createPlayer()` during render. Use the framework bindings, or call it inside `useEffect` / `onMounted` / an action.

### The player is re-created on every React render

You are passing a new `skin()` or `plugins` array on each render. Create them once (module scope or `useMemo`).

### Memory keeps growing in my SPA

Call `player.destroy()` when the view unmounts (the bindings do this for you). It releases engines, listeners, timers and observers. If a third-party plugin leaks, check its `destroy()`.

### Controls don't hide

They hide only while playing, after `idleTimeout` (2500 ms) without pointer or keyboard activity, and never while a menu is open or a control has keyboard focus.

### Styles are missing under a strict Content-Security-Policy

Pass `injectStyles: false` and import `@tomato-player/ui/base.css` plus your skin's `style.css`.

### Still stuck?

Open an issue with a minimal reproduction (the [playground](../examples/playground) is a good starting point), plus your browser, OS and package versions.


<!-- source: docs/migration/README.md -->

# Migration guides

Plyr is deprecated, Vidstack is in security-only maintenance until January 2028, and Media Chrome points new projects elsewhere (see [research](../research/landscape.md)). These guides map familiar APIs to Tomato Player.

## From Plyr

| Plyr | Tomato Player |
| --- | --- |
| `new Plyr('#player', { controls: [...] })` | `createPlayer('#player', { skin: minimal() })`. Pick or compose a skin instead of listing controls. |
| `player.play()` / `pause()` / `togglePlay()` | same |
| `player.currentTime = 10` | `player.seek(10)` |
| `player.volume = 0.5` / `player.muted = true` | `player.setVolume(0.5)` / `player.setMuted(true)` |
| `player.speed = 1.5` | `player.setPlaybackRate(1.5)` |
| `player.source = { type: 'video', sources: [...] }` | `player.setSource([...], { poster, title, tracks })` |
| `player.fullscreen.enter()` | `player.enterFullscreen()` |
| `player.pip = true` | `player.togglePip()` |
| `player.on('ready', fn)` | `player.on('ready', fn)` |
| `keyboard: { global: true }` | `plugins: [hotkeys({ scope: 'global' })]` |
| `previewThumbnails: { src }` | `plugins: [thumbnails({ src })]` |
| `markers: { points }` | `plugins: [chapters({ chapters })]` |
| `storage: { enabled: true }` | `plugins: [persist()]` |
| `i18n: {...}` | `i18n: {...}` (see `defaultStrings` keys) |
| `--plyr-color-main` | `--tp-accent` |
| HLS via `hls.js` + manual wiring | `providers: [hls()]` |
| `player.destroy()` | `player.destroy()` |

## From Video.js (v7/v8)

| Video.js | Tomato Player |
| --- | --- |
| `videojs('id', options)` | `createPlayer('#id', options)` |
| `player.src({ src, type })` | `player.setSource({ src, type })` |
| `player.currentTime(10)` | `player.seek(10)`. Read with `player.state.currentTime`. |
| `player.volume(0.5)` | `player.setVolume(0.5)` |
| `player.paused()` | `player.state.paused` |
| `videojs.registerPlugin('x', fn)` | `definePlugin({ name: 'x', setup(player) {...} })` |
| `videojs.registerComponent` | A `{ el, destroy }` control inside a skin |
| `player.dispose()` | `player.destroy()` |
| `videojs-contrib-quality-levels` | Built in: `state.qualities` and `setQuality()` |
| `.vjs-theme-*` CSS | Skins plus design tokens |

## From Vidstack / Media Chrome

Concepts map almost one-to-one: a store with data attributes, unstyled primitives and layouts.

| Vidstack | Tomato Player |
| --- | --- |
| `<media-player src>` | `<tomato-player src>` or `createPlayer()` |
| `useMediaState('paused')` | `usePlayerState(player, s => s.paused)` |
| `data-paused`, `data-waiting` | Same attribute names on `.tp` |
| Default / Plyr layouts | Skins (`minimal`, `tube`, …) |
| Providers (HLS/DASH) | `provider-hls`, `provider-dash` |

## From ReactPlayer

| ReactPlayer | Tomato Player |
| --- | --- |
| `<ReactPlayer url={u} playing controls />` | `<TomatoPlayer src={u} autoplay skin={minimal()} />` |
| `onEnded={fn}` | `onReady={(p) => p.on('ended', fn)}` |
| `ref.current.seekTo(10)` | `ref.current.seek(10)` |
| `light` (poster mode) | `poster`. Skins show a big play button before start. |

ReactPlayer's YouTube, Vimeo and similar embeds are not providers yet. They are on the [roadmap](../roadmap.md).
